data.title: ICE Review: Canola Slightly Higher, Crude Supports Vegetable Oils
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange made small advances heading into the weekend as rising crude oil supported the vegetable oils.

Ongoing uncertainty in the Middle East raised crude-oil prices and, in turn, brought gains to Chicago soyoil, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil on Friday.

The Saskatchewan canola harvest advanced by seven points at 96% complete as of Oct. 19.

The Canadian Grain Commission reported 158,300 metric tons of canola were exported during the week ended Oct. 18, down from 248,400 tons the previous week. So far this marketing year, 1.377 million tons of canola were exported, compared to 955,300 tons a year ago.

Domestic use for canola during the week was 247,900 tons, less than the 296,100 tons reported the week before. In 2026-27, 2.608 million tons of canola were used domestically, compared to 2.312 million last year.

The Canadian dollar added one-tenth of a U.S. cent compared to Thursday's close.

There were 73,914 canola contracts traded on Friday, compared to Thursday when 92,080 contracts changed hands. Spreads accounted for 44,580 contracts.

data.title: Even the wealthy increasingly want all-inclusive resorts
data.description:
By Bill Peters

Nearly 80% of all-inclusive resorts have become 'luxury or upper upscale,' Bernstein analysts say, as the industry seeks higher-income travelers able to weather inflation

The resort entrance of Sandals Emerald Bay Golf Club on Great Exuma Island in the Bahamas.

As higher costs and global turmoil leave consumers stressed, the fly-and-lie vacation is growing more appealing, even to travel snobs - boosting interest in all-inclusive resorts among higher-end customers and larger hotel operators.

Those resorts were once synonymous with the most generic budget vacations - packed buffets, weak drinks, brightly colored beachfront hotels that vacationers never leave - observed Bernstein analysts in a note on Friday. But all-inclusive resorts have quietly transformed into luxury destinations, according to the note, with Michelin-starred chefs and yoga and wellness retreats, as the travel industry increasingly chases wealthier consumers to offset potentially shrinking profits.

Nearly 80% of the all-inclusive-resort industry has moved into the "luxury or upper upscale" segment over the past two decades, the analysts said. Meanwhile, the increase in Google searches for all-inclusive resorts has significantly outpaced the rise in searches for hotels and cruises, particularly this year, they noted.

The Bernstein analysts said all-inclusive resorts offer a sense of logistical and financial certainty - things that consumers have come back around to, as costs for gas and other essentials have surged against the backdrop of the Iran and Ukraine wars.

"Consumers now face a deluge of choice when planning their trips - with hundreds of potential [restaurants], bars, activities and excursions to choose from," the analysts wrote.

By contrast, an all-inclusive, to a degree, helps do the planning for vacationers, the analysts suggested. Consumers can access a wide range of activities without the exhaustive planning that can come with a trip outside of an all-inclusive, they said.

Similar to the concert industry, the travel industry is increasingly relying on wealthier consumers who are less sensitive to price increases. Higher fuel costs have dinged industry profits and left many travelers frustrated with flight disruptions and higher fares. Both United Airlines (UAL) and Southwest Airlines (LUV) this week cut their profit outlooks.

Meanwhile, bigger companies are turning to all-inclusive resorts to prop up growth. Royal Caribbean (RCL) last month announced it would take a 50% stake in the all-inclusive-resort chain Sandals in an effort to gain more access to wealthier customers - although some analysts questioned whether the move ultimately fit the cruise line's family focus.

Elsewhere, the hotel-chain Hyatt operator (H) last year bought Playa Hotels & Resorts, which runs all-inclusive resorts in Mexico, Jamaica and the Dominican Republic. In 2022, InterContinental Hotels (IHG) and Iberostar Hotels & Resorts signed a partnership intended to expand access to all-inclusive resorts, noting "increasing traveler desire for high-quality experiences and stress-free holidays, particularly post-COVID."

The Bernstein analysts said families were increasingly seeking out hassle-free trips, while younger shoppers were making spending decisions based on convenience.

"Brands have realized consumers are willing to pay for both quality and convenience rather than just the latter, and have started to deliver elevated concepts," they wrote.

The analysts said that all-inclusive resorts offer things that hotel developers like. Longer booking windows and lengthier stays offer steady, predictable business. They also usually cost less to build, the analysts noted, adding that construction in the Dominican Republic and Jamaica costs around 55% to 80% the cost, per room, to build a hotel in the U.S. Labor outside of the U.S., they added, is also generally cheaper.

Unlike hotels in cities, resort properties are also bigger - with sometimes thousands of rooms - allowing them to spread the cost of doing business across more customers.

"The result is that every additional room tends to make the economics more attractive," the Bernstein analysts wrote. "Larger resorts create efficiencies that are difficult for smaller hotels to replicate."

-Bill Peters

data.title: U.S. FDA Approves Subcutaneous Induction Regimen for AbbVie's SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa) for Adults With Moderately to Severely Active Crohn's Disease
data.description:
U.S. FDA Approves Subcutaneous Induction Regimen for AbbVie's SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa) for Adults With Moderately to Severely Active Crohn's Disease

U.S. FDA Approves Subcutaneous Induction Regimen for AbbVie's SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa) for Adults With Moderately to Severely Active Crohn's Disease

PR Newswire

NORTH CHICAGO, Ill., Oct. 23, 2026
  • Now with a new route of induction administration, subcutaneous SKYRIZI supports early symptomatic and endoscopic control with an on-body injector (OBI) device throughout the course of treatment
  • In the pivotal Phase 3 AFFIRM study, subcutaneous (SC) SKYRIZI® achieved superior clinical remissioni and endoscopic responseii at week 12 compared with placebo in patients with Crohn's disease; results were particularly strong in patients without prior advanced therapy failureiii
  • The safety profile of subcutaneous induction was generally consistent with the established SKYRIZI profile in Crohn's disease, with no new safety risks identified
  • FDA also approved an update to the U.S. Prescribing Information warning and precautions across all indications to allow healthcare providers to use clinical judgment when determining whether tuberculosis (TB) testing is needed

NORTH CHICAGO, Ill., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) today announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved a subcutaneous (SC) induction regimen for SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa) for adults with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease (CD)iv. Patients now have the option to start SKYRIZI treatment at home, with induction doses delivered by an on-body injector (OBI) induction pack and then continue using an OBI once every eight weeks throughout the course of maintenance treatment.

"People living with Crohn's disease need treatments that can deliver meaningful disease control from the start," said Roopal Thakkar, M.D., executive vice president, research and development, chief scientific officer, AbbVie. "With the approval of subcutaneous induction, we are building on the strong efficacy of SKYRIZI while giving patients and physicians greater flexibility in how treatment is initiated. This is one more example of how AbbVie continues to advance treatment to better meet the needs of people living with Crohn's disease."

Subcutaneous SKYRIZI Shows High Rates of Clinical Remission and Endoscopic Response by Week 12iii 
This FDA approval is supported by positive results from the Phase 3 AFFIRM trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of SC SKYRIZI versus placebo in patients with moderately to severely active CD.iii SKYRIZI achieved superiority of the co-primary endpoints of clinical remission and endoscopic response at week 12.iii Although the study enrolled a primarily treatment-refractory population, these Phase 3 results were particularly strong within patients without prior advanced therapy failure (advanced therapy-naïve).iii By week 12, nearly three-quarters (74%) of advanced therapy (AT)-naïve patients were in clinical remission (vs. 27% placebo) and these AT-naïve patients achieved endoscopic response at four times the rate of placebo (60% vs. 15%, respectively).iii SC SKYRIZI also had a higher efficacy response in patients who had previously failed advanced therapy.iii

SC SKYRIZI also met secondary endpoints including endoscopic remission and FACIT fatigue scores at week 12 vs. placebo.iii The safety profile of SC SKYRIZI for induction was generally consistent with its known profile in CD, with no new safety risks observed.iii

Together, these results demonstrate market-leading clinical and endoscopic outcomes in advanced therapy-naïve patients that set a high bar in CD. Furthermore, the strength of these subcutaneous results provides a compelling foundation for future clinical trials.

Subcutaneous Treatment With SKYRIZI Offers Fully Self-Administered Therapy From the Start 
The induction dosing regimen with SC SKYRIZI is 720 mg delivered by OBI induction pack at weeks 0, 2, 4 and 8.iii Patients also have the option to start treatment intravenously with 600 mg delivered at weeks 0, 4 and 8.iii Patients can then continue with maintenance dosing starting at week 12 administered by OBI every eight weeks.iii

"When patients and I discuss treatment, they want to know two things: will it work? And how will it fit into their lives?" said Millie D. Long, M.D., MPH, chief, division of gastroenterology and hepatology, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and lead investigator of AFFIRM. "AFFIRM answered the first question, with superior rates of clinical remission and endoscopic response versus placebo during induction with subcutaneous SKYRIZI, particularly in patients new to advanced therapy. This approval answers the second. As a physician who has used the SKYRIZI OBI, I've seen firsthand the convenience it can offer patients. Now with this approval, patients can start treatment at home and continue the same way through maintenance."

Patients Report Satisfaction and Ease of Use in Real World Experience With SKYRIZI OBI
First introduced in 2022 for CD maintenance treatment, the SKYRIZI OBI has demonstrated strong user experience. In a real-world survey of 186 people living with CD, 88% reported AbbVie's OBI easy to use.v In evaluating alternative routes of administration, a patient-reported survey of 352 adults living with IBD found 87% were satisfied or highly satisfied with OBI compared to 71% with an autoinjectorvi, demonstrating patient preference for OBI.

FDA Also Approved Update to Tuberculosis (TB) Language in U.S. Prescribing Information
Additionally, the FDA approved an update to the SKYRIZI prescribing information's warning and precautions language across all approved indications.iii The revised label advises healthcare providers to consider TB evaluation prior to treatment initiation based on clinical judgment.iii This change gives healthcare providers greater flexibility in patient assessment before starting SKYRIZI treatment. There is no mandatory TB test prior to initiating SKYRIZI.

About Crohn's Disease 
Crohn's disease is a chronic, systemic disease that manifests as inflammation within the gastrointestinal tract, most commonly in the area between the small intestine (ileum) and the colon, causing persistent diarrhea and abdominal pain.vii,viii It is a progressive disease, meaning it gets worse over time and may lead to life-threatening complications or surgery.ix,x Because the signs and symptoms of Crohn's disease are unpredictable, it causes a significant burden on people living with the disease—not only physically but also emotionally and economically.xi

About the AFFIRM Studyxii
AFFIRM is a global, Phase 3, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of risankizumab subcutaneous (SC) as an induction treatment in adult patients with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease. Co-primary endpoints were percentage of participants with CDAI Clinical Remission (CDAI < 150) and percentage of participants with endoscopic response at week 12. A total of 274 patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to risankizumab SC or placebo. Key demographics and baseline characteristics were generally balanced between the risankizumab SC and placebo groups; 65% had failed advanced therapies for the treatment of CD before. The study consists of three treatment periods: a placebo-controlled Period A (baseline to week 12) to evaluate the efficacy and safety of risankizumab SC induction treatment, an extended Period B (week 12 to 24) where patients receive blinded or open-label treatments based on their clinical response at week 12, and a 52-week open-label extension Period C where all patients receive the approved risankizumab maintenance treatment.xii More information on this trial can be found at www.clinicaltrials.gov (NCT06063967).xii

Patient Access and Support
AbbVie is committed to helping people access SKYRIZI and other medicines, including offering a patient support program and co-pay card that may reduce out-of-pocket costs to as little as $0 per month for eligible, commercially insured patients. For those with limited or no health insurance, AbbVie offers myAbbVie Assist, a patient assistance program that provides SKYRIZI at no charge to those who qualify. More information about this assistance program can be found at www.AbbVie.com/myAbbVieAssist.

About SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa)
SKYRIZI is an interleukin-23 (IL-23) inhibitor that blocks IL-23 by selectively binding to its p19 subunit. IL-23, a cytokine involved in inflammatory processes, is thought to be linked to a number of chronic immune-mediated diseases.iii SKYRIZI is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis, plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis and Crohn's disease.iii

SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa) U.S. Uses and Important Safety Informationiii
SKYRIZI is a prescription medicine used to treat:

  • moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and children 6 years of age and older who may benefit from taking injections or pills (systemic therapy) or treatment using ultraviolet or UV light (phototherapy).
  • active psoriatic arthritis in adults and children 6 years of age and older.
  • moderately to severely active Crohn's disease in adults.
  • moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in adults.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

What is the most important information I should know about SKYRIZI® (risankizumab-rzaa)?

SKYRIZI is a prescription medicine that may cause serious side effects, including:

Serious allergic reactions:

  • Stop using SKYRIZI and get emergency medical help right away if you get any of the following symptoms of a serious allergic reaction:
    • fainting, dizziness, feeling lightheaded (low blood pressure)
    • swelling of your face, eyelids, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat
    • trouble breathing or throat tightness
    • chest tightness
    • skin rash, hives
    • itching

Infections:
SKYRIZI may lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections and may increase your risk of infections. Your healthcare provider may check you for infections and tuberculosis (TB) before starting treatment with SKYRIZI and may treat you for TB before you begin treatment with SKYRIZI if you have a history of TB or have active TB. Your healthcare provider should watch you closely for signs and symptoms of TB during and after treatment with SKYRIZI.

  • Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have an infection or have symptoms of an infection, including:
    • fever, sweats, or chills
    • cough
    • shortness of breath
    • blood in your mucus (phlegm)
    • muscle aches
    • warm, red, or painful skin or sores on your body different from your psoriasis
    • weight loss
    • diarrhea or stomach pain
    • burning when you urinate or urinating more often than normal

Do not use SKYRIZI if you are allergic to risankizumab-rzaa or any of the ingredients in SKYRIZI. See the Medication Guide or Consumer Brief Summary for a complete list of ingredients.

Before using SKYRIZI, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:

  • have any of the conditions or symptoms listed in the section "What is the most important information I should know about SKYRIZI?"
  • have an infection that does not go away or that keeps coming back.
  • have TB or have been in close contact with someone with TB.
  • have recently received or are scheduled to receive an immunization (vaccine). Medications that interact with the immune system may increase your risk of getting an infection after receiving live vaccines. You should avoid receiving live vaccines right before, during, or right after treatment with SKYRIZI. Tell your healthcare provider that you are taking SKYRIZI before receiving a vaccine.
  • are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. It is not known if SKYRIZI can harm your unborn baby.
  • are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. It is not known if SKYRIZI passes into your breast milk.
  • become pregnant while taking SKYRIZI. You are encouraged to enroll in the Pregnancy Registry, which is used to collect information about the health of you and your baby. Talk to your healthcare provider or call 1-877-302-2161 or visit http://glowpregnancyregistry.com to enroll in this registry.

Tell your healthcare provider about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements.

What are the possible side effects of SKYRIZI?

SKYRIZI may cause serious side effects. See "What is the most important information I should know about SKYRIZI?"

Liver problems may happen while being treated for Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis: A person with Crohn's disease who received SKYRIZI through a vein in the arm developed changes in liver blood tests with a rash that led to hospitalization. Your healthcare provider will do blood tests to check your liver before, during, and at least up to 12 weeks of treatment, and may stop treatment with SKYRIZI if you develop liver problems. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you notice any of the following symptoms: unexplained rash, nausea, vomiting, stomach (abdominal) pain, tiredness (fatigue), loss of appetite, yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice), and dark urine.

The most common side effects of SKYRIZI in people treated for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis include: upper respiratory infections, headache, joint pain, stomach (abdominal) pain, injection site reactions, low red blood cells (anemia), fever, back pain, urinary tract infection, and rash.

The most common side effects of SKYRIZI in people treated for plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis include: upper respiratory infections, headache, feeling tired, injection site reactions, and fungal skin infections.

These are not all the possible side effects of SKYRIZI. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.

Use SKYRIZI exactly as your healthcare provider tells you to use it.

SKYRIZI (risankizumab-rzaa) is available in a 150 mg/mL prefilled syringe and pen, a 55 mg/0.37 mL prefilled syringe, a 600 mg/10 mL vial for intravenous infusion, and a 180 mg/1.2 mL or 360 mg/2.4 mL single-dose prefilled cartridge with on-body injector.

You are encouraged to report negative side effects of prescription drugs to the FDA. Visit www.fda.gov/medwatch or call 1-800-FDA-1088.

If you are having difficulty paying for your medicine, AbbVie may be able to help.

Visit AbbVie.com/PatientAccessSupport to learn more.

data.title: Warhound Launches with $200 Million to Rebuild America's Military Working Dog Supply, Using Advanced Genetics and Defense Technology
data.description:
Warhound Launches with $200 Million to Rebuild America's Military Working Dog Supply, Using Advanced Genetics and Defense Technology

Warhound Launches with $200 Million to Rebuild America's Military Working Dog Supply, Using Advanced Genetics and Defense Technology

PR Newswire

DALLAS and COSTA MESA, Calif., Oct. 23, 2026

Company will produce genetically enhanced working dogs that leverage cybernetics technology to improve health and performance while ending reliance on foreign suppliers

DALLAS and COSTA MESA, Calif., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Warhound, a new defense technology company conceived by American technology entrepreneurs Ben Lamm and Palmer Luckey emerged from stealth with a $200 million seed round. Warhound will rebuild America's domestic supply of elite working dogs for U.S. military forces, law-enforcement, emergency first response teams—a critical national security resource that the U.S. has long relied on foreign countries to provide. Led by CEO David Spirk, the company will reduce dependence on a shrinking European supply chain and strengthen America's ability to protect its own people, infrastructure, and national security interests.

Warhound is modernizing America's working-dog program by delivering a vertically integrated program, combining Colossal's enhanced genetics platform and secure biobanking capabilities of America's top-performing dog arsenal, controlled delivery through cloning with best-in-class training and animal care. Through a partnership, all dogs will be equipped by Anduril's advanced cybernetic Augments, software, and battlefield situational awareness. The company is backed by In-Q-Tel, Sequoia Capital, ARK Invest, Franklin Templeton, 8VC, USIT, Bob Nelsen, Breyer Capital, CAZ Investments, Neogenesis, Builders VC, and Lux Capital among others. Based in Texas, Warhound will operate under the guidance of the American Humane Society which will certify its training programs and support the reunification of retired military working dogs with their former handlers and adoption protocols.

"Palmer, Ben and the Warhound team are exceptional. Sequoia is proud to back them," said Shaun Maguire, Partner at Sequoia Capital.

Warhound is bringing together Colossal's breakthroughs in genetics, cloning, and animal biology with Anduril's advanced defense technology to fundamentally change how America produces, trains, and protects its military working dogs. Colossal's science will help produce healthier dogs with characteristics suited to demanding missions, while Anduril's technology will give dogs and their handlers greater awareness and protection in the field.

"Every day, we ask dogs to put their lives on the line to protect ours. They detect explosives, protect our troops, and run toward dangers that most people are trained to run away from. Yet we're still relying on outdated approaches to breeding and training these extraordinary animals, with too many never making it through the process. We have an opportunity to fundamentally change that. Colossal has spent years pioneering breakthroughs in genetics, cloning, and animal biology, and now we're applying that science to give these dogs the best possible chance at a long, healthy life and a successful mission. If we're going to ask man's best friend to protect America, we owe it to them to use every tool at our disposal to protect them, too," said Ben Lamm.

Since the Army established the K-9 Corps in 1942, military working dogs have served alongside America's armed forces for more than 84 years—detecting threats, protecting service members and supporting missions worldwide. That program has evolved in The United States Department of War's (DOW) Military Working Dog Program, which currently includes 2,200+ working dog teams that are operationally critical for detection and patrol work, and a critical part of the defense infrastructure of the country. More than 80% of U.S. military working dogs are currently acquired from Europe, creating a critical interdependency on foreign nations for an asset the Pentagon itself calls irreplaceable. That dependency is compounding: after a rigorous, roughly three-year acquisition-and-training pipeline, less than half of the dogs procured are ultimately deemed fit for service, meaning the U.S. must source and train roughly 200 dogs today to field 100 working animals tomorrow.

"Man's best friend deserves man's best tech," said Palmer Luckey. 

David Spirk has been named the CEO of Warhound. As a veteran of the United States Marine Corps, he worked as an intelligence specialist with multiple deployments and ultimately served as the Deputy Associate Director of National Intelligence for Afghanistan and Pakistan at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence representing the Intelligence Community at the White House and on Capital Hill. He has an extensive background in the U.S. military, intelligence community, and federal data governance, specifically focused on scaling algorithmic warfare and creating data driven advantages. More recently, he was a Senior Counselor at Palantir Technologies where he focused on expanding the company's software footprints across the U.S. government, allied international partners, and commercial sectors. Previously, he was appointed the First Chief Data Officer (CDO) for the Department of War, where he worked on accelerating the military's data-driven capabilities and was the first CDO for the U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM).

"Our long-term goal is simple: healthier dogs, better-prepared teams, and more service members and first responders coming home safely. Leading Warhound, and strengthening America's working-dog capabilities, is an opportunity to apply my experience to a mission I care deeply about: protecting people and helping the animals who support them," said David Spirk. "My focus is building a team that can turn scientific advances into capabilities that work in the field."

Building Healthier, More Capable Working Dogs to Protect Both Dogs and People
The concept of Warhound was conceived years ago by Palmer and Ben after a discussion at Peter Diamandis' Moonshots Summit. Military working-dog programs face a costly challenge: more than half of candidate dogs fail to complete training, while reliance on overseas breeders leaves the United States dependent on a constrained foreign supply chain. Warhound was created to improve that system—producing fewer dogs with a greater likelihood of remaining healthy, completing training, and succeeding in their missions.

Warhound dog-and-handler teams will also connect Anduril's integrated capabilities—including eye and ear protection and Eagle Eye technology—will help safeguard working dogs, their handlers and the wider unit while supporting safer, more effective missions.

"For millennia, people have selectively bred dogs to be companions and helpmates. Modern biotechnology gives us a more precise way to shape some of their traits, thus improving both the work dogs do and their own health and well-being," said Alta Charo, Warren P. Knowles Professor Emerita of Law and Bioethics at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. "The Warhound project offers the possibility of improving working dogs' health and welfare while supporting the lifesaving work they do. But we still must look carefully at who benefits, what risks the animals bear, and how concern for animal welfare translates into practice through careful evaluation of the evidence, meaningful oversight, and responsibility for the dogs throughout their lives, including retirement. The American Humane Society brings valuable experience through its military working dog reunification efforts and Pups4Patriots program. That experience provides a foundation, but public trust has to be earned through the care we provide and the commitments we keep."

Animal welfare is central to the program. By improving health, durability, and training success, Warhound will significantly reduce washouts, limit the number of dogs unnecessarily entering intensive training and enable safer, more effective missions. Technologies and therapeutics developed through the program will also be made available to all dogs and ultimately improve the health of all dogs, not only those serving alongside America's service men and women. Together, these capabilities will establish a secure domestic supply of military working dogs while giving American service members healthier, more capable canine partners.

"Working dogs are extraordinary animals whose courage and loyalty save lives," said Dr. Robin Ganzert, President and CEO of American Humane Society. "We owe these dogs a commitment to their well-being that matches their service to us. What excites me about Warhound is the opportunity to make health, welfare, and exceptional care fundamental to a working-dog program from the very beginning. Success means helping these dogs thrive throughout their lives—from training and active service to the loving, dignified retirement every canine hero deserves."

Warhound is built to take today's level of performance and make it better: using cutting edge engineering and technology, on American soil, from American companies, without the wait times, price volatility, or geopolitical exposure of a foreign supply chain.

About Warhound
Warhound is a Texas-based defense technology company building a secure domestic supply of healthier, more capable working dogs for the U.S. military, law enforcement and emergency responders. Conceived by Palmer Luckey and Ben Lamm, Warhound combines biotechnology licensed from Colossal Biosciences with advanced training and Anduril's cybernetic augments and software. The company aims to reduce reliance on foreign suppliers, improve canine health and performance, and enhance safety for dogs and their handlers. Animal welfare is central to Warhound's mission, with a commitment to lifelong care from birth through training, service and retirement. To follow along, please visit: warhound.com.

About Anduril
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company that builds autonomous systems and a common operating layer to give the United States and its allies a persistent advantage in sensing, decision-making, and force projection.

About the American Humane Society
The American Humane Society is the country's first national humane organization and a global leader in animal welfare. Founded in 1877, American Humane has been at the forefront of protecting animals, rescuing them from cruelty, abuse, and natural disasters, and setting the gold standard in science-based welfare certifications. The organization oversees prominent programs including the iconic "No Animals Were Harmed®" film and television certification, the American Humane Certified™ farm and zoo standards, military working dog reunifications, and the Pups4Patriots™ service dog program. Learn more at americanhumane.org. 

About Colossal Biosciences
Colossal was founded by emerging technology and software entrepreneur Ben Lamm and world-renowned geneticist and serial biotech entrepreneur George Church, Ph.D., and is the first to apply CRISPR technology for the purposes of species de-extinction. Colossal creates innovative technologies for species restoration, critically endangered species protection and the repopulation of critical ecosystems that support the continuation of life on Earth. Colossal is accepting humanity's duty to restore Earth to a healthier state, while also solving for the future economies and biological necessities of the human condition through cutting-edge science and technologies. To follow along, please visit: www.colossal.com.

data.title: 'She's living the dream': My stepmother said I can buy my childhood home for $850,000. Is she taking advantage of me?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'My late father bought our house for $250,000 in the 1990s'

"She said if my dad wanted me to have it, he should have arranged that before he died." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

My late father bought our house for $250,000 in the 1990s. By the time he died, it was worth about $850,000, mostly because it's spacious and in a good neighborhood. He left it to my stepmother, whom he married a few years after my mom died. She is now 74. They were together for 18 years. She took care of him through the whole illness, which I don't take lightly.

Dad told me more than once that the house would be mine someday. My stepmother now wants to sell and move somewhere smaller. She's living the dream in Miami. I offered $700,000. That's $200,000 under market, but I thought it was fair, given that she would skip agent fees and it would be a quick, clean sale. I'd have to stretch to do it, but I could manage.

She was really offended, and she told me as much. She said she's paid the property taxes and the repairs for years (she put a new roof on in 2021). She also said she spent a big chunk of her own savings on my father's care and that the house is basically her retirement plan, and that she can't just hand me $200,000 because I'm sentimental.

Don't miss: My wife says we can't afford to retire. I vetoed her $8,000 trip to Italy. We're in our 60s and have $4 million. Do I keep working?

The $200,000 discount

That's a fair point, and I told her so. What I can't get past is that a few years ago she gave her daughter $200,000 toward a house, and that is how (and why) I came up with the $200,000 haircut on my father's home. I brought that up, and she said things were different then, and pointed out that I have a good job and can buy my own place.

She said if my dad wanted me to have it, he should have arranged that before he died. As my girlfriend at the time said, "Yes, she really went there." That comment really stung. He trusted her with everything, and it feels like his wishes just evaporated. She says she honored him by caring for him and that I'm discounting everything she sacrificed.

I could, of course, walk away and buy somewhere else. I've even looked at a couple of listings. But it wouldn't be the same, and I'd always feel like the house slipped away from our family. I know that my stepsister's place has a sauna in the basement, and I'd bet anything that my stepmother helped pay for that too. Not that I'm keeping score. (OK, I know I am a little.)

Am I being unreasonable?

The Stepson

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: My wife never went back to work after raising our kids. Do I have to share my retirement savings 50/50?

You can't force someone to sell you a house that never legally belonged to you.

Dear Stepson,

Don't allow steam from your stepsister's sauna to cloud your vision. You can grieve the loss of your childhood home without assigning blame.

What's more, you can't force someone to sell you a house that never belonged to you in the first place. Your childhood home, legally and morally, belonged to your father. Even though you grew up there, that doesn't give you the right to a life estate or a $200,000 discount on the purchase price because your stepmother gave her daughter $200,000 toward the down payment on her own home. What's more, selling a house to a family member below fair market value can create a gift of equity equal to the price difference, which the IRS may treat as a taxable gift.

Your late father made a promise that he did not keep, could not keep or decided not to keep. That was his responsibility. It's not your stepmother's job to make good on your father's promises. Whether he made a will leaving her the house or whether she inherited the house through state intestate laws, the end result is the same: She legally owns the house, and she has the right to live there or sell it to whomever she wants.

It is your belief that your father's wishes "evaporated." But wishes, promises and/or intentions evolve, and perhaps he realized that he wanted to take care of his wife of nearly two decades, and die with the knowledge that she would always have a roof over her head. It would have been better to have discussed those plans with you rather than leaving you in a kind of limbo, wondering if he truly wanted to leave his estate to his wife. Chances are, he did.

That does not mean this is an easy or pleasant situation for you. You have an emotional attachment to this property, and you regard your stepmother as an interloper, inheriting a property where your own mother probably once lived. It's a tough break for you and your siblings, if you have any. You made your stepmother an offer and she declined. She may be thinking about her own retirement and financial future.

Don't miss: 'I don't feel sorry for myself': I'm 64 and will be renting for the rest of my life. Is that so bad?

Passing judgment

Two decades is a long time to spend with someone. She met your father when she was in her 50s, and she's now rightly concerned about medical costs, if she needs nursing home care, especially if she does not have long-term care insurance, or any other kind of life insurance. This house may be the only asset she has, and downsizing will give her a cushion as she heads towards her 80th birthday in six years. That's quite a reality check.

I'm heartened that you realize that taking care of your father was no small deal for your stepmother. Who will take care of her if she sells you this house for $650,000 and runs out of money? Will you drive her to hospital appointments and spend hours a day with her, making sure that she takes her medication and pays her bills, and has enough to eat? That might sound dramatic, but getting older often comes with health complications.

One could argue that you both "went there." She "went there" by telling you your father wanted her to have his house. You "went there" by using emotional leverage, whether or not you believe it in your heart to be valid, to persuade her to sell this house to you on the cheap. By doing so, you are, whether you realize it or not, also passing judgment on her marriage of 18 years to a man she probably loved very much. You both spoke plainly. That's OK. Just know it's 50/50.

If you want this house, put in an offer when it is listed for sale. If she does get more than one offer and, say, one party offers $50,000 more, she may still decide to sell you the house (and maybe not even mention that she is selling it to you at less than the other offer). Remember, if she gets $950,000 rather than $850,000 - a real possibility if it's a cash buyer and it's a sought-after neighborhood - she would have been giving you a $300,000 discount if she agreed to your proposal.

All is fair in love, second marriages, legal beneficiaries and real estate. Just don't overstretch yourself financially for the sake of nostalgia.

Related: 'People in the U.S. need to wake up': As a mortgage loan officer, I rejected applications from wealthy couples. Here's why.

Check out The Moneyist's private Facebook group, where members help answer life's thorniest money issues. Post your questions, weigh in on the latest Moneyist columns or email The Moneyist at qfottrell@marketwatch.com.

More columns from Quentin Fottrell:

'I am a pretty cautious person': My financial adviser wants me to invest $350,000 in a UAE data center. Is this risky?

My sister moved in with our mother, 78, and now says she deserves the $925,000 family home. Is she right?

-Quentin Fottrell

data.title: Commercial HVAC Expert Brian Sinkler of Green Bay, WI Stresses Pre-Summer Inspection for HelloNation
data.description:
Commercial HVAC Expert Brian Sinkler of Green Bay, WI Stresses Pre-Summer Inspection for HelloNation

Commercial HVAC Expert Brian Sinkler of Green Bay, WI Stresses Pre-Summer Inspection for HelloNation

PR Newswire

GREEN BAY, Wis., Oct. 23, 2026

GREEN BAY, Wis., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What is the one hvac check every business should complete before summer begins? A HelloNation article provides the answer, pointing to refrigerant levels, coil cleaning, and airflow testing as the foundation of preventive maintenance. The feature highlights Green Bay professional Brian Sinkler of Sinkler Heating and Cooling, Inc., who explains how a pre-summer inspection protects commercial hvac systems from strain, breakdowns, and rising energy costs. Readers can review the full details in a HelloNation article.

The article notes that commercial hvac systems are among the hardest-working pieces of equipment in a business. They operate for long hours every day, keeping staff and customers comfortable regardless of conditions outside. Summer creates the greatest challenge, with higher temperatures and humidity pushing systems to their limits. Without preventive maintenance, this demand can quickly turn into failure.

Checking refrigerant levels is the most important step. Refrigerant absorbs indoor heat and releases it outdoors. The HelloNation article explains that low refrigerant levels prevent proper cooling, forcing longer cycles and higher energy costs. Running with insufficient refrigerant also strains the compressor, one of the most expensive components to replace. Detecting and correcting this issue before summer helps avoid poor performance and costly repairs.

Coil cleaning is another critical part of a pre-summer inspection. Evaporator and condenser coils collect dirt and debris, which blocks heat transfer. According to the HelloNation article, when coils are coated, the system works harder to cool, raising utility bills and wearing down parts. Professional coil cleaning restores efficiency, ensuring the system operates at full capacity during peak heat.

Airflow testing completes the foundation. Blocked ducts, weak fans, or clogged filters prevent conditioned air from reaching all parts of the building. This creates uneven comfort and forces the system to run longer, wasting energy. The HelloNation article shows how airflow testing identifies these issues and ensures smooth circulation throughout the property.

Preventive maintenance avoids breakdowns at the busiest time of year. For retail businesses, warm conditions may drive customers away. Offices lose productivity when staff cannot work in comfortable conditions. Companies storing perishable goods face even greater risks from cooling failures. A pre-summer inspection ensures reliable performance when cooling is most critical.

Energy costs are another major factor. The HelloNation article stresses that commercial properties face their highest energy bills during peak summer. By confirming refrigerant levels, completing coil cleaning, and performing airflow testing, businesses reduce energy costs while improving results. These savings provide a return on investment month after month.

The article also highlights how preventive maintenance extends equipment lifespan. Motors, fans, and compressors suffer under strain when systems are neglected. Small issues left unchecked can accelerate wear and shorten useful life. By addressing them early, businesses avoid premature replacement and the high expense of new equipment.

Another advantage is avoiding emergency repair calls during peak demand. When cooling fails in the middle of summer, service technicians are in short supply. Delays and higher repair costs often follow. A pre-summer inspection provides peace of mind, reducing the chance of emergencies and securing reliable operation ahead of time.

For larger commercial buildings, inspections often include thermostat calibration, zoning system checks, and building management system adjustments. The HelloNation article explains that these steps improve energy efficiency and maintain comfort across multiple zones. Properly tuned controls allow businesses to manage costs while delivering consistent conditions throughout the property.

Some businesses view maintenance as an expense, but the article emphasizes the opposite. Preventive maintenance is an investment that lowers long-term costs. Skipping a pre-summer inspection often leads to higher energy bills, emergency service fees, and lost revenue from downtime. In contrast, scheduled service ensures stability, efficiency, and consistent comfort.

The HelloNation feature concludes that summer strain on commercial hvac systems is unavoidable, but breakdowns are not. With refrigerant levels checked, coil cleaning performed, and airflow testing completed, businesses can depend on their systems through the hottest months. Preventive maintenance delivers comfort, lowers energy costs, and protects operations.

In Green Bay, HVAC Expert Brian Sinkler of Sinkler Heating and Cooling, Inc. helps businesses prepare for these challenges. His approach to preventive maintenance aligns with the HelloNation article, stressing the value of preparation, efficiency, and reliability in commercial hvac service.

For the full feature, read The One HVAC Check Every Business Needs Before Summer. The article highlights the expertise of HVAC Expert Brian Sinkler of Green Bay and his practical advice through HelloNation.

About HelloNation
HelloNation is a premier media platform that connects readers with trusted professionals and businesses across various industries. Through its innovative "edvertising" approach that blends educational content and storytelling, HelloNation delivers expert-driven articles that inform, inspire, and empower. Covering topics from home improvement and health to business strategy and lifestyle, HelloNation highlights leaders making a meaningful impact in their communities.

data.title: BioVid Launches Mimetics™, AI Research Audiences Built on How Physicians Reason and Decide
data.description:
BioVid Launches Mimetics™, AI Research Audiences Built on How Physicians Reason and Decide

BioVid Launches Mimetics™, AI Research Audiences Built on How Physicians Reason and Decide

PR Newswire

BRISTOL, Pa., Oct. 23, 2026

Modeling physician response patterns and behavior, showing an 80–90% match with real physicians on content, reasoning, and emotion. 

BRISTOL, Pa., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BioVid, a life science consultancy, today announced the launch of BioVid Mimetics™, a research platform that gives pharmaceutical teams mimetics: synthetic physician audiences modeled on how those audiences reason and decide. Its respondent models are grounded in BioVid's proprietary MindSet Modeling™ program, large-scale, multi-specialty surveys of practicing physicians that measure the mindsets shaping how they process information, make judgments, and decide. The models are aligned with secondary data on clinical practice, moving beyond generic AI role-play to model the decision logic behind treatment choices.

 Like a mimetic drug, each BioVid mimetic is tested against the original: real physicians.

Prescribing data shows what physicians choose, not why. Pharma teams now face more of those "why" questions than research budgets and timelines can absorb. BioVid Mimetics™ applies the social and behavioral science of clinical judgment to model how physicians interpret evidence, weigh benefit against risk, and decide when they know enough to act.

The name comes from pharmacology, where a mimetic earns trust by doing the work of the original molecule. Every BioVid mimetic is tested against that standard, bringing the firm's long-standing commitment to science-based research to a new method.

"At BioVid, we've always believed that better commercial decisions start with a deeper understanding of human behavior," said Peggy Hirtle, CEO of BioVid. "Our goal was never simply faster or cheaper respondents. It was to reflect how physicians actually reason, with the same scientific rigor clients already trust from BioVid. Mimetics is a new way to put human understanding to work, never a replacement for it."

"A synthetic respondent can sound right and still reason wrong. The real test is whether it reasons the way the audience does," said Marco Barcella, Executive Director, Product & Technology at BioVid. "Where the decision warrants, we run the same study with a human cohort and a mimetic cohort and compare the findings, the reasoning, and the mental and emotional responses directly. Clients see where mimetic findings hold and where human research should lead."

In BioVid's validation work to date, mimetic and human cohorts have shown an 80% to 90% match on content, reasoning, and emotion across thousands of parallel tests.
